title: U.S. House · Oregon's 3rd District
area: Most of Multnomah County (inner and east Portland), northeastern Clackamas County, and all of Hood River County.

context.text: Incumbent Maxine Dexter defeated Jessica Salas and Andrew Castilleja with 89.1% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Loran Ayles ran unopposed for the Republican nomination.

summary.text: Maxine Dexter is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 3rd Congressional District, which she has represented since 2025. A pulmonary and critical-care physician, she spent more than 15 years at Kaiser Permanente before serving in the Oregon House of Representatives from 2020 to 2024, where she chaired the Housing and Homelessness Committee.

background.text: Born in Seattle, Washington, in 1972; grew up in the Pacific Northwest in a working-class family and, according to her official biography, took a union job at Albertsons at 16 and became the first in her family to graduate from college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and communications (1997) and an M.D. (2001) from the University of Washington; Ballotpedia lists her as triple-boarded in internal medicine, pulmonology and critical care medicine.
Moved to Portland with her husband and two children after medical training and practiced for over 15 years as a lung and critical-care physician at Kaiser Permanente.
Elected by her physician group to leadership roles and became the first woman to chair the Board of Directors at Northwest Permanente.
Has been a member of the Oregon Medical Association and a trustee of the Tualatin Hills Park Foundation.

Was appointed in 2020 to Oregon House District 33 (succeeding Mitch Greenlick) and served through 2024; as chair of the House Housing and Homelessness Committee she led passage of a multi-billion-dollar housing and homelessness bill, and also worked on abortion access, addiction treatment, public lands and gun-violence legislation.
Was elected to the U.S. House in 2024, succeeding Earl Blumenauer.
In Congress, serves on the Veterans' Affairs and Natural Resources committees and is Ranking Member of the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

positions.summary: Her official issues page says she supports defunding and dismantling ICE.
positions.quote: Dexter supports defunding and dismantling ICE.

positions.summary: Her official issues page says she believes everyone has the right to make health care decisions about their own bodies, including access to abortion services.
positions.quote: She knows that access to the full spectrum of reproductive health services— from birth control to abortions—is critical to building healthy, thriving communities.

positions.summary: Her official issues page calls her a defender of Medicaid who is pushing back against efforts to cut or restrict access to it.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Dexter is a strong defender of Medicaid, which provides lifesaving care to children, low-income families, people with disabilities, and older Americans.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Subcommittee on Health) and is Ranking Member of the Natural Resources Committee's Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

As an Oregon state representative, chaired the House Housing and Homelessness Committee and sponsored legislation to address the state's housing and homelessness crisis, addiction treatment, abortion access, and gun violence.
